items.pronunciation_notes: One long syllable beginning with a य glide: yaad.

learn.title_en: Three verbs, three different kinds of remembering
learn.explanation_en: याद is the richest collocation in this module because it takes three verbs and each means something distinct. याद आना is remembering by itself — मुझे याद आया, it came back to me. याद करना is deliberate: memorising, or thinking of someone. याद रखना is keeping something in mind for later. English uses remember for all three and Hindi will not, so the verb you choose says what kind of remembering you mean. याद is feminine and flagged.

examples.note: It came to me — आना is intransitive, so the perfective works now.
रखना for holding on to something deliberately.
The auxiliary is dropped after नहीं, as usual.

common_error.why_en: याद करना is deliberate recall or memorising. For missing someone, Hindi uses याद आना with the person in the possessive.

practice.question: याद
practice.explanation_en: याद is memory or the state of remembering, and it is feminine.

game.question_en: Which verb goes with याद when something comes back to you on its own?
game.explanation_en: याद आना — it comes to you. करना is deliberate recall and रखना is keeping it in mind.

items.pronunciation_notes: The श्क cluster runs together with no vowel between: mush-kil.

learn.title_en: मुश्किल is both the adjective and the noun
learn.explanation_en: मुश्किल means difficult, and it is unmarked so it never changes: सवाल मुश्किल है, बात मुश्किल है. The same word is also a feminine noun meaning a difficulty — मुश्किल में हूँ, I am in trouble — and context tells you which. That double life is common with Arabic and Persian borrowings in Hindi. Its opposite is आसान, easy, which is also unmarked, so neither of the pair will ever ask you for an ending.

examples.note: A masculine subject, and the adjective is unchanged.
A feminine subject, and still मुश्किल.
आसान is the opposite, and also unmarked.

common_error.why_en: मुश्किल does not take an ending for gender. Adding -ी to make it feminine produces a word that does not exist.

practice.question: मुश्किल
practice.explanation_en: मुश्किल is difficult, and the same word is also a noun meaning a difficulty.

game.explanation_en: मुश्किल होना. Adjectives of state take होना throughout this module.

items.pronunciation_notes: Long ii then an aspirated kh with no vowel between it and the न: siikh-naa.

learn.title_en: सीखना, पढ़ना, समझना — three different things
learn.explanation_en: सीखना is to learn, in the sense of acquiring a skill you did not have. पढ़ना is to read or to study, the activity you do at a desk. समझना is to understand, the moment it clicks. English blurs the first two constantly — I am learning Hindi and I am studying Hindi are near-identical — and Hindi keeps them apart. मैं हिंदी सीख रहा हूँ says you are acquiring the language; मैं हिंदी पढ़ रहा हूँ says you are reading it right now.

examples.note: The continuous — सीखना is transitive, so the perfective waits for Module 9.
जल्दी means quickly and does not change.
चाहना takes the plain infinitive in front of it.

common_error.why_en: Not wrong, but it means you are reading Hindi at this moment. For acquiring the language, the verb is सीखना.

practice.question: सीखना
practice.explanation_en: सीखना is to learn a skill. सिखाना is to teach, formed with the same long aa that made चलाना from चलना.

game.question_en: Which verb means acquiring a language rather than reading it?
game.explanation_en: सीखना is acquiring the skill. पढ़ना is reading or studying, and समझना is understanding.

summary.recap_en: The school block is complete at twelve words. याद is the module's richest collocation — आना for spontaneous recall, करना for deliberate memorising, रखना for keeping in mind — and सीखना, पढ़ना and समझना stay separate where English blurs them.
summary.next_up_en: Next: shopping and money, starting with the shop, the cash and the price.

items.pronunciation_notes: The first syllable is short and the second long: du-kaan.

learn.title_en: दुकान is feminine, and it is a Class 5 noun
learn.explanation_en: दुकान is a shop, feminine and flagged since the consonant ending predicts nothing. It is Class 5, so it does not change in the singular and takes दुकानों in the oblique plural. Like any destination it takes no postposition with जाना — दुकान जाओ — but with से it means from the shop, which is what you use when saying where you bought something.

examples.note: The destination takes no postposition, as always with जाना.
बड़ी is feminine, which proves दुकान is.
The Class 5 oblique plural takes plain -ों.

common_error.why_en: दुकान is feminine. The consonant ending gives no clue at all, which is why it carries a flag.

practice.question: दुकान
practice.explanation_en: दुकान is a shop, feminine, and it declines like किताब.

game.explanation_en: दुकान जाना — and the destination takes no postposition.

items.pronunciation_notes: The first syllable holds a diphthong close to the vowel in English 'pie': pai-saa.

learn.explanation_en: पैसा in the singular is a coin — historically a hundredth of a rupee. Money in general is पैसे, the plural, and that is what you will use almost every time: पैसे दो, pay up; मेरे पास पैसे नहीं हैं, I have no money. English treats money as singular and Hindi does not, so the verb goes plural too. पैसा is Class 1, so it becomes पैसे in the plural and पैसों before a postposition.

examples.note: The plural is the ordinary form for money.
मेरे पास is the have construction from Module 6, and हैं is plural.
पैसों is the oblique plural before की.

common_error.why_en: The singular would mean you do not have one coin. Money in general is plural in Hindi, and the verb follows.

practice.question: पैसा
practice.explanation_en: पैसा is money, and the plural पैसे is the form you will use almost always.

game.question_en: Which verb goes with पैसे when you pay?
game.explanation_en: पैसे देना — to pay. पैसे लेना would be taking money from someone.

items.pronunciation_notes: The dotted क़ is made deep in the throat, further back than a plain क: qii-mat.

learn.title_en: क़ीमत, and the question you will actually ask
learn.explanation_en: क़ीमत is the price, feminine and flagged. In a shop you are more likely to hear यह कितने का है — how much is this, literally this is of how much — than the more formal क़ीमत क्या है. Both work. क़ीमत also means value in the abstract sense, so किसी चीज़ की क़ीमत is what something is worth. Note the dotted क़, which is pronounced further back in the throat than a plain क.

examples.note: कितने is oblique before का — the everyday way to ask a price.
ज़्यादा is unmarked and means more or excessive.
बढ़ना is intransitive, and रही agrees with the feminine plural.

common_error.why_en: One price is singular. The plural क़ीमतें would need हैं, but the singular takes है.

practice.question: क़ीमत
practice.explanation_en: क़ीमत is the price or value, and it is feminine.

game.question_en: Which question actually asks a price in a shop?
game.explanation_en: यह कितने का है — literally this is of how much. More common than asking क़ीमत directly.

summary.recap_en: Money is plural in Hindi — पैसे, with a plural verb — where English treats it as singular. दुकान and क़ीमत are both feminine with consonant endings that predict nothing, and the everyday way to ask a price is यह कितने का है rather than anything containing क़ीमत.
summary.next_up_en: Next: expensive, cheap and the discount you will try to get.

items.pronunciation_notes: The nasal hum sits on the middle syllable: ma-haṁ-gaa.

learn.title_en: A marked adjective, so it agrees
learn.explanation_en: महँगा ends in -ा, which makes it a marked adjective and one of the few in this module that actually changes: महँगा, महँगी, महँगे. Most of Module 8's adjectives have been unmarked and invariable, so this pair is where the Module 6 agreement rules come back into play. यह किताब महँगी है, because किताब is feminine. Getting it wrong here is more visible than usual, because the words it describes are the ones you say out loud in a shop.

examples.note: A masculine or unspecified subject.
किताब is feminine, so the adjective takes -ी.
A masculine plural noun, so the adjective takes -े.

common_error.why_en: महँगा is marked, so it agrees. After a run of invariable adjectives it is easy to stop checking.

practice.question: महँगा
practice.explanation_en: महँगा is expensive, and it agrees with the noun it describes.

game.explanation_en: किताब is feminine, so the marked adjective takes -ी.

items.pronunciation_notes: The स्त cluster runs together with no vowel between: sas-taa.

learn.explanation_en: सस्ता is cheap, marked, and agrees exactly as महँगा does: सस्ता, सस्ती, सस्ते. Worth noting that it does not carry the sneer English cheap can — calling something सस्ता is usually a compliment about the price rather than a complaint about the quality. For poor quality you would say घटिया. The two words to have ready in a shop are बहुत महँगा है and कुछ सस्ता दिखाइए, show me something cheaper.

examples.note: A compliment about the price, not a complaint.
दुकान is feminine, so the adjective takes -ी.
दाम is a masculine plural word for price, so the adjective takes -े.

common_error.why_en: दुकान is feminine, and सस्ता is a marked adjective, so it has to follow.

practice.question: सस्ता
practice.explanation_en: सस्ता is cheap in the sense of inexpensive, with no suggestion of poor quality.

game.explanation_en: दुकान is feminine, so the marked adjective takes -ी.

items.pronunciation_notes: Aspirated chh at the front and a retroflex ट at the back: chhuuṭ.

learn.title_en: छूट मिलना — a discount is received
learn.explanation_en: छूट is a discount, feminine and flagged. Its verb is मिलना, to be received, which is intransitive — so छूट मिली, I got a discount, works in every tense including the perfective. That makes it one of the few shopping words you can use in the past right now. छूट देना also exists and is what the shopkeeper does. The related verb छूटना means to be left behind, which is why a train you miss is छूट गई.

examples.note: मिलना is intransitive, so the perfective is available now.
The future, and मिलेगी agrees with the feminine छूट.
देना from the shopkeeper's side, with respectful plural agreement.

common_error.why_en: छूट is feminine, so the perfective is मिली. The consonant ending predicts nothing.

practice.question: छूट
practice.explanation_en: छूट is a discount, feminine, and it is received with मिलना.

game.question_en: Which verb goes with छूट from the buyer's side?
game.explanation_en: छूट मिलना — the buyer receives it. छूट देना is what the shopkeeper does.

summary.recap_en: महँगा and सस्ता are marked adjectives and agree, which is a change after a long run of invariable ones. छूट takes मिलना from the buyer's side and देना from the seller's — the same two-sided pattern as परीक्षा and क्लास.
summary.next_up_en: Next: buying, selling, and the person on the other side of the counter.

items.pronunciation_notes: The dotted ख़ is far back in the throat and the ii is long: kha-riid-naa.

learn.title_en: ख़रीदना, and where you bought it takes से
learn.explanation_en: ख़रीदना is to buy, and the place you bought from takes से: मैं दुकान से ख़रीदता हूँ. That is the same से you met in बस से and स्टेशन से दूर — it covers from in all its senses. ख़रीदना is transitive, so its perfective needs ने and is not available yet. For small everyday purchases Hindi often uses लेना instead, which is gentler and shorter: दूध लो, get some milk.

examples.note: से for the source, and दुकान is oblique before it.
The future, which is safe with any verb.
The continuous, with तुम taking रहे and हो.

common_error.why_en: में would mean you are inside the shop doing the buying. The source of a purchase takes से.

practice.question: ख़रीदना
practice.explanation_en: ख़रीदना is to buy, and it is transitive.

game.question_en: Which postposition marks where you bought something?
game.explanation_en: दुकान से ख़रीदना — the source takes से.

items.pronunciation_notes: A clear e in the first syllable and no vowel before the न: bech-naa.

learn.title_en: बेचना, and who you sell to takes को
learn.explanation_en: बेचना is to sell, and it completes the pair with ख़रीदना. Note the postpositions: you buy from a place with से and you sell to a person with को — मैं उसे बेचता हूँ. That is the same split you met with पूछना taking से and देना taking को, and it holds generally. Anything moving away from you towards a person uses को; anything coming from a source uses से.

examples.note: The habitual — बेचना is transitive, so the perfective waits.
बेचती agrees with दुकान, which is feminine.
नहीं in front of the verb, and the future is safe.

common_error.why_en: You sell to a person, so को — which fuses into उसे. से would mean you are selling from him.

practice.question: बेचना
practice.explanation_en: बेचना is to sell, and it pairs with ख़रीदना.

game.question_en: Which postposition marks the person you sell to?
game.explanation_en: उसे बेचना — selling to a person takes को, while buying from a source takes से.

items.pronunciation_notes: Four syllables with the length on the last: du-kaan-daar.

learn.title_en: The -दार suffix makes the person who holds something
learn.explanation_en: दुकानदार is a shopkeeper — दुकान plus -दार, a Persian suffix meaning one who holds or keeps. It is productive, so once you see it you can read a whole family of words: ज़िम्मेदार, one who holds responsibility; समझदार, one who has understanding; ईमानदार, honest. All are masculine by default and all are Class 2, so nothing changes in the plural. As with any person you ask, दुकानदार takes से with पूछना.

examples.note: पूछना takes से for the person asked.
Plural agreement for a stranger, as a mark of politeness.
The same -दार suffix, on समझ rather than दुकान.

common_error.why_en: पूछना always takes से for the person asked. को belongs with देना and बेचना.

practice.question: दुकानदार
practice.explanation_en: दुकानदार is a shopkeeper, built from दुकान plus the suffix -दार.

game.question_en: Which postposition goes with दुकानदार when you ask them something?
game.explanation_en: दुकानदार से पूछना — पूछना takes से for the person asked.

summary.recap_en: You buy from a source with से and sell to a person with को, which is the same split as पूछना and देना. The suffix -दार makes the person who holds something, and it is productive enough to let you read words nobody has taught you.
summary.next_up_en: Next: rupees and the bill, and a conversation at the counter.

items.pronunciation_notes: Three light syllables with the length only on the last: ru-pa-yaa.

learn.title_en: With any number above one, use the plural
learn.explanation_en: रुपया is a rupee, masculine and Class 1, so its plural is रुपये. That plural is what you use with every number above one — दो रुपये, सौ रुपये — and English speakers often leave it singular by mistake. Note that this is a genuine plural rather than the general-money plural you saw in पैसे: रुपये are countable and पैसे is money in the mass. In the oblique it becomes रुपयों, as any Class 1 noun does.

examples.note: A number above one, so the plural.
The का construction for price, agreeing with the masculine यह.
The तुम imperative of देना.

common_error.why_en: Any number above one takes the plural. English says two rupee in Indian speech sometimes, but Hindi does not.

practice.question: रुपया
practice.explanation_en: रुपया is a rupee, masculine, with the plural रुपये.

game.explanation_en: Any number above one takes the plural रुपये.

items.pronunciation_notes: One short syllable with a light l: bil.

learn.title_en: बिल देना works from both sides
learn.explanation_en: बिल is borrowed from English, masculine and Class 2. Its verb is देना, and unusually the same phrase works in both directions: the waiter gives you the bill and you give the money, so बिल दीजिए means bring me the bill and बिल दो can mean pay up. Context sorts it out. The Hindi alternative for settling a bill is बिल चुकाना, which is unambiguous but more formal.

examples.note: The polite imperative — one of the four irregulars from Module 7.
The same कितने का shape used for any price.
ज़्यादा is unmarked and never changes.

common_error.why_en: करना is the default guess and it is wrong. A bill is given, whichever direction it is travelling.

practice.question: बिल
practice.explanation_en: बिल is a bill or invoice, masculine, and unchanged in the plural.

game.explanation_en: बिल देना — and the same phrase works from both sides of the counter.

items.pronunciation_notes: Both words end on a long ii, which is what marks the feminine agreement.

learn.title_en: Two adjectives and a verb, all agreeing with different things
learn.explanation_en: The first two lines use महँगा and सस्ता with no noun in sight, so they take the default masculine — you are pointing at something unnamed. The last two switch to छूट, which is feminine, so both मिलेगी and थोड़ी take -ी. Three agreement decisions in four short lines, each answering to a different word. This is also a real bargaining exchange: asking for छूट is normal and expected in most Indian shops that do not display fixed prices.

common_error.why_en: छूट is feminine, so both the adjective and the verb take -ी. Getting the gender wrong costs two words here.

practice.question: छूट मिलेगी?
practice.explanation_en: The future of मिलना, agreeing with the feminine छूट.

game.question_en: Listen to the last line. Which word is missing?
game.explanation_en: छूट is feminine, so the marked adjective takes -ी.

summary.recap_en: रुपये takes the plural with any number above one, and बिल takes देना from both sides of the counter. The bargaining exchange puts three agreement decisions in four lines, each answering to a different word.
summary.next_up_en: Next: the last of the shopping block, then food and cooking.
